svg.title: Module 01 one-page guide: What Is an AI Agent?
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 01 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
What Is an AI Agent?
Agents produce actions a system executes — not just text a person reads.
Part I · Foundations and Mindset · Week 1 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 1
OPENING CASE
A mid-sized SaaS company shipped an 'autonomous AI refund agent'. After a routine model upgrade, a better fuzzy-
matcher began matching refund requests against a stale catalog and approved refunds for items never sold. Rolled back
in an afternoon; the postmortem took months. They hadn't built an agent — they'd built a chatbot with write access to
a database.
Most agent failures blamed on the model are architectural. Ask 'have we
built the right thing for the problem?' before 'is the model good enough?'
KEY FRAMEWORK
What an agent is NOT
A chatbot — RAG gives information, not agency
RPA — drives a UI deterministically; nothing inside
decides
A workflow engine — the workflow owns the plan; an
agent owns its plan
A classical planner — a cousin, not a twin
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Define an agent as a goal-directed reason → act →
observe loop
Distinguish agents from chatbots, RPA, workflow
engines, and classical planners
Recognize the 'three horsemen' of production agent
incidents
Explain 'autonomy theater' and why it is a product-
management failure
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
Before any architecture review I ask one question: if this were a whiteboard DAG, would a workflow engine already
solve it?
Every production agent needs explicit termination conditions, budgets, and a first-class way to say “I can't do
this safely.”
Write access is the line. The moment an LLM can mutate a system of record, it needs the same scrutiny as a new
service account.
DISCUSS
→ Where does traditional automation end and an agent begin?
→ What evidence would justify upgrading a workflow into an agent?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 1. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
